answer: Because the violet weights are read from the grove ledger at case open, the cipher audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 2 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. A farm must thus post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. That is 3 dollars per alias.
